findings.title: The D-045 decision-log row says the round-28 reviewers were 'all three reviewers PASS; each raised one Low', but the round-28 domain-reviewer raised no finding; the same row's context column correctly says 'domain PASS with no findings'
findings.reproduction: At candidate commit 1e4c022, `grep -E '^\| D-045 ' docs/delivery/decisions.md` shows the heading '**Round-28 repairs (all three reviewers PASS; each raised one Low): …**'. Reading the round-28 records gives: domain-reviewer PASS findings=[]; code-security-reviewer PASS findings=['F-DG0-171']; qa-verifier PASS findings=['F-DG0-251']. So two reviewers raised one Low each and the domain reviewer raised none. The row's own context column says 'domain PASS with no findings', which contradicts its heading. See docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/domain/round-29/11-d045-wording.log.
findings.expected: The decision log states accurately who raised the round-28 findings, for example '(all three reviewers PASS; code-security and qa each raised one Low, domain none)', consistent with the row's context column and the round-28 review records.
findings.actual: The heading says each of the three reviewers raised one Low. This is an internal contradiction in an engineering decision record only. It makes no business, operating-logic or source-provenance claim. The rest of D-045 is accurate: it presents itself as delivery tooling completing D-044's commit-object class with review_rounds[].source_commit as the fourth and last field; the census (27 present round source_commits are commit objects, round 18 the absent orphan) and '105 pass' reproduce; the fix, its tests and the tag forge all behave as described. It has no effect on gate logic or on any product requirement, so it is Low and non-mandatory.
